issues.text: h1 renders in the Newsreader fallback, not Exposure/Exposure-20. Computed font-family is 'Exposure, Exposure-20, Newsreader, ...' but no Exposure font file exists in the project, so the browser falls through. Figma's Exposure is a heavy, low-contrast serif; the rendered Newsreader is a high-contrast Didone with visibly thinner stems. Measured: line 1 'AI compute at' is 603px wide vs 674px in Figma and line 2 is 781px vs 858px (both ~10% narrow) at identical 108px/108px metrics. This is the section's dominant element. Ship the Exposure webfont; if it cannot be licensed, raise the fallback weight (~600-700) and widen tracking so the mass approximates the reference.

Vessel/sail imagery is far darker and more saturated than Figma. Mean RGB over the vessel block (y700-1150, x250-900) is 138,165,171 in the build vs 197,215,212 in the reference; a tone sweep shows build midtones ~60-80 levels below the reference while highlights match, i.e. the atmospheric haze that washes the sails in Figma is missing. Sky and water elsewhere are within ~5-10 levels, so only the vessel plate is wrong. Note hero-sky.png / hero-vessel.png both failed to download during asset fetch (Figma rate limit) - re-fetch the real plates, or lift the shadows/midtones of the substitute so the sails read pale blue-white, not solid blue.

Lead paragraph wraps to 5 lines instead of Figma's 4 ('Autonomous vessels take AI' / ... / 'tape is thin.' vs 'Autonomous vessels take AI compute' / ... / 'plentiful, and the red tape is thin.'). Cause is font width, not font-size: the strong run 'Autonomous vessels' measures 220px vs 204px in Figma (+7.8%) because no Matter font file is present and the stack falls back to Inter. Knock-on: the CTA pill sits at y650 instead of y612, ~38px below the design. Ship Matter, or widen the lead measure so the Figma line breaks survive.

CTA pill measures ~181px wide vs 174px in Figma; the label 'Read the white paper' runs 140px vs 134px. Same Inter-instead-of-Matter root cause as the lead reflow; pill height, 999px radius, 12/20px padding and the rgba(25,25,25,0.08) hairline are all correct.

A dev-tooling badge reading '5 Issues' renders over the hero at bottom-left (x20-125, y845-880). It is the framework dev overlay, not build markup, but the 5 logged issues are worth a look outside this section.

Geometry is otherwise pixel-exact: wordmark 157x28 at x642/y148, h1 line boxes at y182-269 and y282-379, lead ink top at y480 with 28px leading, 12px white side gutters, square top / rounded bottom stage corners, split-opacity lead (100% / 48%) all match the reference.
Same wrong display typeface as desktop: h1 renders in the Newsreader fallback instead of Exposure. A missing font is a token violation judgeable without a tablet mock.
Same vessel tone problem as desktop - the sails render as solid mid-blue rather than the pale, hazed blue-white of the reference plate.

The lead paragraph and CTA land squarely on the vessel's sails at this width, so the 48%-opacity run ('the wide-open ocean, where clean energy and') sits at low contrast over painted detail. Nudging the lead block up ~40px would put it back on open sky.

Responsive adaptation itself is sound and no tablet mock exists to contradict it: lead column centres under the title per the 768-1023 rule, headline holds its two-line break, no overflow, gutters and bottom radius preserved, hulls stay in frame.
Same wrong display typeface as desktop: h1 renders in the Newsreader fallback instead of Exposure.

The non-breaking space between 'the' and 'maritime' is missing from the h1. Mobile breaks the headline 'AI compute at the' / 'maritime edge.' - with the U+00A0 the spec requires ('the maritime'), it would break 'AI compute at' / 'the maritime edge.', which still fits the 330px measure. Desktop only matches by coincidence of measure, so the fix is in the markup, not the CSS.
Same vessel tone problem as desktop - sails render as solid mid-blue instead of the reference's pale, hazed blue-white.
Lead paragraph overlaps the masts across all five lines; the 48% run over painted sail detail is the weakest-contrast text on the page. Consider shifting the lead block above the mast tops.

No mobile mock exists; the adaptation is otherwise clean - no horizontal overflow at 390px, ~620px stage, headline scales down sensibly, CTA keeps a 40px tap target, hulls stay in frame, gutters and bottom radius preserved.

summary: Layout and spacing are essentially pixel-exact against the 1440 mock, but the hero is let down by two asset-level gaps the section file cannot fix alone: neither Exposure nor Matter is present in the project, so the headline renders as Newsreader (~10% narrow, far lighter) and the lead reflows to 5 lines in Inter, while the un-fetched vessel plate renders ~60 levels darker than the reference.
